name: Battle of Hastings
note: Accounts differ on the exact site where the English stood (the abbey site or Caldbec Hill). The woods on the English flanks and the marshy ground in front of them are named in the accounts, which do not say exactly where they lay. The direction in which the beaten English fled is not given. The place of the English rally at the Malfosse is not known; it is drawn on their side of the field.

phases.title: The two armies take their ground
phases.text: The English formed a shield wall at the top of the slope. William drew up archers in front, spearmen behind them in three divisions, and kept his cavalry in reserve.
phases.quote: The English formed a shield wall, with the front ranks holding their shields close together or even overlapping to protect from attack.

phases.title: The Norman archers shoot uphill
phases.text: The battle opened with the Norman archers shooting uphill at the English shield wall. The slope turned their arrows aside or sent them over the top of the hill, and they had little effect.
phases.quote: The battle opened with the Norman archers shooting uphill at the English shield wall, to little effect.

phases.title: The spearmen go forward
phases.text: William sent the spearmen forward to attack the English. They met a barrage of spears, axes and stones and could not force an opening in the shield wall.
phases.quote: William sent the spearmen forward to attack the English.

phases.title: The cavalry advance in support
phases.text: The Norman cavalry came up to support the infantry. They too failed to make any headway against the shield wall.
phases.quote: The infantry was unable to force openings in the shield wall, and the cavalry advanced in support.

phases.title: A general retreat begins
phases.text: The Normans fell back in a general retreat, blamed on the Breton division on William's left. A rumour that William had been killed added to the confusion.
phases.quote: a general retreat began, blamed on the Breton division on William's left. A rumour started that William had been killed

phases.title: Some of the English pursue
phases.text: Some of the English left the wall to pursue the fleeing invaders. William rode through his forces, showing his face and shouting that he was still alive.
phases.quote: The English forces began to pursue the fleeing invaders, but William rode through his forces, showing his face and yelling that he was still alive.

phases.title: William counter-attacks
phases.text: William rode through his forces, showing his face and shouting that he was still alive. He led a counter-attack against the pursuing English, and the men who had left the wall were overwhelmed.
phases.quote: He then led a counter-attack against the pursuing English forces; some of the English rallied on a hillock before being overwhelmed.

phases.title: The cavalry feign flight
phases.text: After a probable lull William tried a new tactic: cavalry sent against the shield wall, then drawn back to pull the English into further pursuits. It was said to have been used twice.
phases.quote: If the Normans could send their cavalry against the shield wall and then draw the English into more pursuits, breaks in the English line might form.

phases.title: The assault on a thinned shield wall
phases.text: The feigned flights did not break the line but probably thinned out the housecarls, who were replaced by men of the fyrd, and the shield wall held. Archers were used again before and during an assault by cavalry and infantry led by William.
phases.quote: Archers appear to have been used again before and during an assault by the cavalry and infantry led by William.

phases.title: Harold dies and the English collapse
phases.text: Harold died late in the battle, though the accounts of how he died contradict each other. His death left the English leaderless and they began to collapse, and the Normans pursued the fleeing troops.
phases.quote: Harold's death left the English forces leaderless, and they began to collapse.

phases.title: A last stand at the Malfosse
phases.text: Except for a rearguard action at the Malfosse, the battle was over. There some Englishmen rallied and seriously wounded Eustace of Boulogne before the Normans defeated them.
phases.quote: except for a rearguard action at a site known as the "Malfosse", the battle was over.
